cues.en: In the last course module, we started working on our course project and as part of that project we
built a couple of components because that is what Svelte is all about, or at least it's a very important
part of Svelte.
It is how you structure your svelte applications.
Now when you have a look at the application we started building, you'll notice that we have a couple
of warnings here on the right, which in the end have to do with props that we didn't set a value on
those.
And in addition, there are a couple of unsolved problems.
For example, when we would click one of these buttons here in the meetup item, how could we communicate
this click up to a parent component?
Or more importantly, how could we create our own custom event, something like show details or maybe
delete if we had a delete button?
How can we create custom events and not just work with the built in ones click and so on, but with
our own events to propagate information up from a component to the component where we're embedding it.
Like here in the app component where we use our meetup grid.
What if we are interested in something that changes a meetup here in the app component, even though
the click happens in a deeply nested component in this meetup item component.
These are some of the problems we'll have a look at in this module, where you will learn how to write
your components more efficiently and some extra nice tricks that help you with building components that
really can communicate with each other and that allow you to build a nicely structured and highly reactive
application.
